references.text: The Preacher warns against making vows without fulfilling them, stating that it is better not to make a vow than to make one and fail to keep it.
Describes the laws concerning vows and oaths, emphasizing that a man who makes a vow to the Lord must keep his word and do all he has promised.
Provides detailed rules on how vows to the Lord should be fulfilled, especially regarding the valuation of persons dedicated to the Lord.
Encourages making vows to the Lord and keeping them, showing that God expects vows to be fulfilled.
Encourages offering sacrifices of thanksgiving to God and fulfilling vows to the Most High.
The psalmist expresses his commitment to fulfill his vows to God, confirming the importance of keeping what one has promised.
Warns against making a vow hastily and only later thinking about what one has promised.
Paul cut his hair at Cenchreae because he had taken a vow, showing that vows to God were also taken seriously in the New Testament.
Jesus teaches about oaths and vows, emphasizing the importance of keeping what one has said to the Lord.
